items.title: Massive 176,000-Square-Foot Grocery Store Opens in Mississauga with Global Food as Its Draw
items.summary: Food World Plus, described as Ontario's largest grocery store, opened to shoppers on Oct. 30 at 50 Matheson Blvd. East in Mississauga. According to the store, its 176,000-square-foot facility is built around global food, offering products and ingredients from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East and South Asia. The store said it aims to give shoppers in Mississauga's diverse community access to ingredients they might otherwise need to visit several specialty grocers to find. Beyond its international aisles, Food World Plus is positioning itself as a one-stop destination with a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and in-house butcher. The store said its meat department includes a dedicated halal section, with meat sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards from delivery through to the cuts prepared for customers. Mayor-elect Alvin Tedjo attended the grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford and later welcomed the new store to the city in a social media post.

items.title: Incoming Mississauga mayor pushes for provincial funding during first Queen's Park visit
items.summary: During his first visit to Queen's Park since being elected mayor of Mississauga, Alvin Tedjo says he's pushing for more financial support from the province to help him address some key priorities.

items.title: Mississauga Inclusive-Leadership Expert Named Finalist for Speaker Slam's Top Honour
items.summary: Karen Craggs, a Mississauga-based inclusive leadership expert and keynote speaker, is one of 14 finalists competing for Speaker Slam's Inspirational Speaker of the Year title on Nov. 21. According to organizers, the Toronto-based competition draws entries from qualifying tournaments held across North America throughout the year, with the strongest speakers advancing to the Grand Slam Inspirational Speaking Final at CBC's Glenn Gould Studio. Organizers said this year's finals mark the 10th annual edition of what they describe as North America's largest competition of its kind. The winner will receive $5,000 in cash along with a prize package valued at up to $50,000, organizers said. Speaker Slam co-founder Dan Shaikh said in a news release that this year's theme, built around the idea of a catalyst and how change shapes a person into someone who changes things for others, describes Craggs' life's work. Shaikh noted that Craggs is well known for championing inclusive leadership, a management style focused on valuing and empowering diverse team members.

items.title: Streetsville Councillor Says New Operator May Be Lined Up for Shuttered Franklin House
items.summary: The Franklin House, a longtime restaurant and bar in one of Mississauga's most historic buildings, is currently closed, leaving residents in Streetsville wondering what comes next for the landmark. According to Ward 11 Councillor Brad Butt, he has heard a new operator may be preparing to take over the business and could reopen it soon. Butt said he has not been contacted directly by anyone involved in the business and does not know whether a new operator would keep the Franklin House name or its current restaurant format. He said it remains unclear whether the space would continue to run as it has, or shift to a different format. Butt also pointed to challenges that come with operating in the historic building, including a relatively small main-floor dining area and limited space upstairs. He said the upper floor is better suited to occasional private functions than regular restaurant service, while the basement presents another challenge due to flooding risk.

items.title: Mississauga Man's Decade of Steady Lotto Play Pays Off with $100,000 Encore Win
items.summary: Corey John, a Mississauga man who has played the lottery regularly with OLG for about a decade, is $100,000 richer after his Sept. 19 Lotto 6/49 ticket matched six of seven Encore numbers in exact order. According to the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation, the winning ticket was purchased at a Petro-Canada gas station on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Mississauga. John told OLG officials his previous biggest win was $500, calling that one exciting but saying this win is a little more exciting. He said the moment he found out was completely unexpected, and that his fiancee didn't believe him at first when he told her the news. John, who plays Lotto 6/49 twice weekly and always adds Encore, picked up his cheque at the OLG Prize Centre in Toronto. He said he has plans for the windfall, including a vacation and possibly a renovation to his house.

items.title: Relocated Beavers Return to Mississauga's Lisgar Area, Prompting Renewed Monitoring
items.summary: Beavers that the City of Mississauga relocated away from Sixteen Mile Creek and Osprey Marsh last fall and winter have returned to the area, according to Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden. The city said it had removed a number of beaver dams and beavers from the Lisgar community in the city's northwest, near the Milton border, after the dams caused drainage and water flow problems near the creek and marsh. McFadden said residents began reporting beaver sightings again this past spring, prompting her and city staff to keep a close eye on the situation while they searched for a longer-term solution. She told constituents at the time that additional attention was being paid to the matter in the coming weeks. McFadden said in a recent update that the beavers, among the largest living rodents in the world, continue to reside along Sixteen Mile Creek running through Lisgar.

items.title: Mississauga Spells Out Snow-Clearing Timelines Ahead of 2026-2027 Winter Season
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says its winter operations team will be available around the clock this season to keep roads, sidewalks, bus stops and bike routes safe for travel. According to the city, crews prioritize major roads, high-use sidewalks, transit routes, emergency routes and pedestrian crossings first, using tools such as salt brine and sidewalk and windrow plows. The city said major roads, bus stops and priority sidewalks are typically cleared within 12 to 24 hours of a snowfall ending, while residential roads and sidewalks are cleared within 24 to 36 hours, though major storms or back-to-back weather events can extend those timelines. Sidewalks in front of homes are cleared only after snowfall has stopped, the city said. Mississauga added that it may declare a Citywide Winter Parking Restriction when needed to let crews clear snow safely, during which parking on city streets is banned and temporary and residential paid parking permits are suspended. The city said that starting this winter, the restriction will also apply to vehicles parked in 15-hour parking exemption zones for the first time.

items.title: Buyer-Friendly Market Pushes Mississauga's Lowest October Home Sale to $265,000
items.summary: Zoocasa says the least expensive home sold in Mississauga last month went for $265,000, as buyer-friendly market conditions pull some sale prices well under $300,000 across the Greater Toronto Area. According to the real estate brokerage, the city's average home price dipped 5 per cent month-over-month to $929,600 in September, though that figure remains below the $969,501 average recorded in September 2025, per Toronto Regional Real Estate Board data. Zoocasa said the most affordable sales are typically condo units going for under $500,000. Among the five cheapest homes sold in October, the brokerage listed a two-bedroom corner unit in the new M City development, which has floor-to-ceiling windows, a wrap-around balcony and building amenities including a skating rink and rooftop terrace, selling for $432,000 over its $399,000 asking price. Another listed sale was a one-bedroom-plus-den suite in City Centre with more than 700 square feet of space, nine-foot ceilings and access to indoor and outdoor pools, a fitness centre and 24-hour concierge service.
